MR . JUSTICE SANJAY KUMAR ORAL JUDGMENT Date: 31-10-2017 This application under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure has been filed to quash the order dated 07.06.2011 passed by the Sub Divisional Judicial Magistrate, Patna City in connection with C.B. Case No. 06 of 2011.

entities.text: Sub Divisional Judicial Magistrate, Patna City
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The learned Magistrate as per impugned order took cognizance for the offence under Sections 16(1)(a)(1) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954.
2. Heard the learned counsel for the petitioners and the learned A.P.P. for the State.
3. The above C.B. Case No. 06 of 2011 was registered on the prosecution report of Civil Surgeon-cum-Chief Medical Officer, Patna, which is based on the report of Food Inspector, Patna.

The Patna High Court Cr.Misc. No.48439 of 2014 dt.31-10-2017 Food Inspector conducted raid at the Rail Head Point Fatuha, District- Patna on 26.08.2010 and found Chirai Cook Salt stored for sale and sold, which does not confirm to the prescribed quality laid down under the P.F.A. Rules 1955 and therefore, it was adulterated within the meaning of Section 2(1a) and (m) of the P.F.A.
Rules 1955.

The Food Inspector got salt analyzed from the combined Food and Drug Laboratory,
Agamkuan, Patna which is part of F.I.R.

The Public Analyst has reported that the salt was analyzed and it did not confirm to the prescribed standard of quality laid down under the P.F.A. Rules and Rupesh Bhala & Anr vs The State Of Bihar on 31 October, 2017 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/184936255/
1

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: hence, the same was adulterated.
4. The contention of the learned counsel for the petitioners is that the petitioners are not the owners of the said salt.
The petitioner No. 1 was employee of the firm 'M/s Bhala-Brothers' owned by Sri Banwarilal Bhala.

The petitioner No. 1, Rupesh Bhala, is the son of Radheshyam Bhala and not the son of Banwarilal Bhalla, which finds support from the copy of income tax return, which is Annexure-2 of the supplementary affidavit.

It has been further contended that the petitioner No. 2,
Rupesh Kumar Sinha was working agent for collecting money from the market.
He is a registered employee with employer State Insurance Corporation.
These two petitioners had no concern with the firm M/s Bhala Brothers and so the impugned order is fit to be quashed.
Patna High Court Cr.Misc. No.48439 of 2014 dt.31-10-2017 5.
The learned A.P.P. for the State on the other hand opposed the submission.

6. On perusal of impugned order, I find that the learned Magistrate on being satisfied with the report of Public Analyst which is part of prosecution report submitted by the Civil Surgeon-cum- Chief Medical Officer, Patna took cognizance for the offence under the relevant provision of the Prevention of Adulteration Act.

The defence of the petitioners and reliability of petitioners'
document cannot be examined at the stage of cognizance.
The petitioners will have opportunity at subsequent stage.
7. In the facts and circumstances of the case, I do not find any merit in this criminal miscellaneous application.
This criminal miscellaneous application is accordingly dismissed.

(Sanjay Kumar, J) ajay gupta/-
